steps.body: You can tell how many solutions a system has **before** solving, by comparing the lines. **Different slopes** → they cross once → **one solution**. **Same slope, different intercept** → parallel → **no solution**. **Same slope and intercept** → the same line → **infinitely many**.
Different slopes cross once. Predict, then make them equal and watch.

predict.prompt: You are about to make the two rates equal. The single crossing will…

options.label: Be gone — no crossing at all
Move somewhere else on the grid
Slide off the edge, still out there somewhere

predict.reveal: Gone. Equal rates means the lines never close on each other, so they hold a constant gap and never meet — not further along, and not off the edge of the grid either. Only if their starting values match as well do the two become one line.

widget.prompt: Drag the point to where y = x + 1 and y = −x + 5 cross. Then grab a line itself and tilt it until the two rates match — watch what happens to the crossing, and bring it back before you check. The steppers below set exact values.
widget.successFeedback: (2, 3) — and it checks in both: 2 + 1 = 3 and −2 + 5 = 3. Now make the two rates equal and watch this crossing leave.
widget.offLine1Feedback: Your point is not on line 1. A solution has to sit on both lines at once.
widget.offLine2Feedback: On line 1, but not on line 2. The solution is the single point the two lines share.
widget.degenerateSystemFeedback: Equal rates, so there is no single crossing to mark. Two cases live here, and both are worth seeing. If the starting values differ, the lines are parallel: they hold that same gap forever, so they never meet further out either — there is nowhere off the screen for them to cross. If the starting values match, the two equations describe one line, and every point on it satisfies both — infinitely many solutions, not none. Change either rate to bring a single crossing back.

explanationVariants: Both have slope 2 but intercepts 1 and −3 — parallel lines that never meet, so no solution.
Equal slopes, different y-intercepts means parallel: no crossing, no solution.

widget.prompt: How many solutions does the system y = 2x + 1 and y = 2x − 3 have?

options.label: No solution
options.feedback: Yes — same slope 2, different intercepts: parallel lines that never meet.

options.label: Exactly one
options.feedback: One solution needs different slopes. These share slope 2, so they're parallel: no solution.

options.label: Infinitely many
options.feedback: That needs identical lines. Same slope but different intercepts means parallel: no solution.

steps.body: **Parallel** is the no-solution case. Equal slopes tilt the lines the same way; different y-intercepts start them at different heights. They march alongside each other forever and never cross — so there's no point that satisfies both.

widget.prompt: How many solutions does the system y = 4x + 2 and y = 4x + 2 have?

options.label: Infinitely many
options.feedback: Yes — the two equations are identical, so every point on the line satisfies both.

options.label: Exactly one
options.feedback: They're the same line, so they overlap everywhere — infinitely many solutions, not one.

options.label: No solution
options.feedback: Same slope AND same intercept means one line, not parallel. Every point works: infinitely many.

steps.body: When both equations describe the **same line**, every point on it satisfies both — **infinitely many** solutions. Watch for equations that look different but are the same line in disguise; comparing slope and intercept settles it.
Match each system to its solution count.

widget.prompt: Compare slopes and intercepts, then match each system.

pairErrors.feedback: Same slope 3 but different intercepts — parallel lines, so no solution, not infinitely many.
These are the identical line, so every point works: infinitely many, not none.

widget.missFeedback: Different slopes → one; same slope, different intercept → none; same line → infinitely many.
widget.successFeedback: You read all three off the slopes and intercepts — no solving needed.

explanationVariants: Both are y = −x + 4 — the same line — so every point satisfies both: infinitely many.
Same slope and same intercept means one line, hence infinitely many solutions.

widget.prompt: How many solutions does the system y = −x + 4 and y = −x + 4 have?

options.label: Infinitely many
options.feedback: Yes — identical equations, one line, so every point on it solves the system.

options.label: Exactly one
options.feedback: The lines coincide, so they share every point, not just one: infinitely many.

options.label: No solution
options.feedback: They're the same line, not parallel. Every point works: infinitely many.

explanationVariants: Both have slope 1 but intercepts 4 and −4 — parallel, so no solution.
Equal slopes, different intercepts: parallel lines, no crossing.

widget.prompt: How many solutions does the system y = x + 4 and y = x − 4 have?

options.label: No solution
options.feedback: Yes — slope 1 for both, but intercepts 4 and −4 differ: parallel, no solution.

options.label: Exactly one
options.feedback: Equal slopes can't cross once. Different intercepts make them parallel: no solution.

options.label: Infinitely many
options.feedback: That needs identical intercepts too. Here 4 ≠ −4, so parallel: no solution.

explanationVariants: Both have slope 1/2 but intercepts 3 and −1 — parallel, so no solution.
Equal slopes (1/2 = 1/2), different intercepts: parallel lines, no solution.

widget.prompt: How many solutions does the system y = (1/2)x + 3 and y = (1/2)x − 1 have?

options.label: No solution
options.feedback: Yes — both slopes are 1/2, but intercepts 3 and −1 differ: parallel, no solution.

options.label: Exactly one
options.feedback: Compare the slopes: both 1/2, so they're parallel, not crossing. No solution.

options.label: Infinitely many
options.feedback: Same slope but different intercepts (3 vs −1) means parallel, not the same line: no solution.

hints: Compare the slopes first: both are 1/2.
Equal slopes mean parallel or identical — check the intercepts.
Intercepts 3 and −1 differ, so parallel: no solution.

steps.body: Slopes and intercepts reveal the solution count at a glance.
takeaways: Same slope, different intercept → no solution (parallel).
Same slope and intercept → infinitely many (same line).

concept.body: Compare the two lines. Different slopes cross once → one solution. Same slope but different intercepts are parallel → no solution. Same slope and same intercept are one line → infinitely many.

explanationVariants: Slopes 2 and 5 differ, so the lines cross once: exactly one solution.
Different slopes always give a single crossing point.

widget.prompt: How many solutions does the system y = 2x + 1 and y = 5x − 2 have?

options.label: Exactly one
options.feedback: Yes — slopes 2 and 5 differ, so they cross exactly once.

options.label: No solution
options.feedback: That's the parallel case, which needs equal slopes. Here 2 ≠ 5, so they cross once — one solution.
